headline: Energy Markets Slump Despite Fresh Middle East Supply Anxiety
paragraphs: Natural gas jumped 11.30 percent over the week as winter cold risks mounted and uncertainty from the Iran war impacted the liquefied natural gas industry. Crude oil also suffered heavy weekly losses, with Brent down 6.60 percent and WTI falling 5.35 percent, as prices declined sharply following US midterms, though a partial rebound occurred due to lingering Middle East supply risks and Strait of Hormuz tensions.

Precious metals experienced downward pressure as a strengthening US dollar and broader inflation concerns weighed on markets, pushing gold below the 4,000 dollar threshold to 3,988.40 dollars per ounce, a 1.04 percent daily drop and a 3.04 percent weekly decline. Conversely, palladium gained 1.89 percent on the day, while silver rose 0.94 percent, helping lead a partial rebound alongside ongoing industrial demand.

Copper edged up 0.55 percent as AI worries faded and persistent shortages in China drove up industry costs. The euro held at 1.1072 against the US dollar, maintaining steady exchange rates for Irish business transactions as domestic inflation reached 4.3 percent in October driven by high energy prices.
